Naegler, T., Simon, S., Klein, M. and Gils, H.C. (2015). Quantification of the European industrial heat demand by branch and temperature level. International Journal of Energy Research, 39(15), 2019-2030. https://doi.org/10.1002/er.3436

NO TECHNOLOGY PARAMETERS EXTRACTED. A statistical top-down estimate of EU28 final energy demand for heat in 2012 by industry branch, member state and temperature level (two approaches: <100/100-400/>400 degC and <100/100-500/500-1000/>1000 degC). It has no process-, equipment- or technology-level data: no specific energy consumption, efficiency, cost or process temperature for any technology; branch temperature shares are taken from German studies (AGFW 2005; Wagner and Unger 2002) and appear only as charts (Fig. 1, 3), so they cannot be loaded as printed numbers. Numbers it does print: EU28 industrial heat 8150 PJ (approach 1) and 8518 PJ (approach 2) for 2012; approach 1 by level <100 degC 2077 PJ, 100-400 degC 2214 PJ, >400 degC 3859 PJ (Table III, p.2024); approach 2 SH/HW <100 degC 1161 PJ, process heat <100 degC 1027 PJ, 100-500 degC 1785 PJ, 500-1000 degC 1679 PJ, >1000 degC 2865 PJ (Table III); national totals for 28 states (Table III); industry final energy by branch (Tables I-II, EU28 11547 PJ Eurostat, 11085 PJ IEA); text shares: >1000 degC is 34% of industrial heat (steel 48%, non-metallic minerals 27%), 500-1000 degC 20% (chemicals 45%, minerals 22%, steel 21%), 100-500 degC 21% (paper and print 42%), process heat <100 degC 12% (food 31%, chemicals 22%, paper 15%), SH/HW 14%; five branches (steel, chemicals, minerals, paper, food) hold 83% of process heat demand; quantified uncertainty about 7% EU28 total, up to 20% by level, up to 30% by country. Useful only as a cross-check of the temperature-band shares by branch (to-get need: Rehfeldt bands cross-check); these sector statistics could go to a reference table, not to technology extraction. Printed page numbers 2019-2030 (PDF page = printed - 2018).
Zuhlsdorf et al. (2019, zuhlsdorf_2019_001) cites it for the 20% share of 100-500 degC heat in large heat-user countries (>30% in Sweden, Finland, Portugal).
